title: Improving First Nations water security through governance
authors: Alcantara, Longboat, Vanhooren
exclusion_reason_detail: Theoretical/conceptual framework paper; authors state explicitly they build a framework prior to data collection rather than present empirical evidence.

title: Public Utility Ownership in 19th-century America: The "Aberrant" Case of Water
authors: Masten, Scott E.
exclusion_reason_detail: Outcome is waterworks ownership form (public vs. private), not a household access/connection/exclusion outcome -- does not map onto this review's outcome hierarchy.

title: Fecal sludge management system approach for establishing policy framework in urban areas of Vientiane Capital, Lao PDR
authors: Sidlakone S.; Ichiki A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Examines fecal sludge collection/transport/treatment chain and regulatory capacity for managing it, not household-level legal/administrative access to a connection. All surveyed households already have on-site sanitation. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention; 8 other FSM papers in the pool may share this issue.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Comprehensive Analysis of Community and Rural Aqueduct Systems
authors: Salazar-Gámez L. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: AI-driven diagnostic study of 14 community aqueduct systems (Pasto, Colombia). Unit of analysis is the aqueduct system, not the household; outcomes are provider-side technical performance and the provider's own regulatory/tax compliance, not household legal/administrative access mechanisms. Core contribution is a GenAI diagnostic methodology.

title: Flows against the current: governance and politics of wastewater reuse in Valle Alto, Bolivia
authors: Saldías C.; Echeverría I.; Vargas V.; Saavedra O.
exclusion_reason_detail: Rich qualitative governance/institutional-bricolage study, but population/exposure is farmers accessing treated wastewater for agricultural irrigation, not household connection to a networked water/sanitation service. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention.

title: Financial insecurity among sanitation workers and its impacts on safe service reliability: a case study of the Arusha depot manual emptying group
authors: Kimwaga R.; Magambo H.; Ndezi T.
exclusion_reason_detail: Population/exposure is sanitation workers' financial insecurity affecting their own service delivery behavior, not households navigating legal/administrative access to a service. Labor-economics study of the supply side.

title: Co-Creating an Intersectional Water Justice Toolkit and Documentary in Cape Town, South Africa
authors: Puvaneyshwaran D. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Describes co-design of an advocacy toolkit and documentary film; reports no empirical outcome relevant to access, connection, service availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. A knowledge-mobilization/practice resource, not an empirical access study.

title: Assessing urban water security in Awash River Basin, Addis Ababa, and its surrounding towns using Integrated Urban Water Security Index
authors: Legass A.M. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Composite water-security index study dominated by hydrology, water-quality chemistry, GIS mapping, and climate modeling. Governance appears only as a single survey satisfaction item; no legal/administrative access mechanism is analyzed as an exposure variable.

title: Effectiveness of emergency WASH strategies in disaster-prone areas of Africa: a systematic review
authors: Chirwa E.; Mwalwanda A.; Soko M.; Mbakaya B.C.
exclusion_reason_detail: Systematic review of emergency WASH intervention effectiveness on health/disease outcomes (cholera) during disasters, not on access/connection/administrative outcomes. No legal or administrative access mechanism examined.

title: Responsible leadership and sustainability performance of health and sanitation projects: the mediating role of resilience
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: PLS-SEM survey of project staff/implementers (n=520) across 86 health/sanitation projects in Uganda; exposure is leadership style, outcome is organizational sustainability performance -- not household legal/administrative access. Part of a related Kyambade et al. cluster on project-level sustainability/governance (see also RA8E99F31040E, R26FD0045CAAA, R5FB1EE86B250) that may share this issue -- not yet screened.

title: Water for All: A Strategic Assessment of Drinking Water Management at Cox's Bazar of Bangladesh in the Light of SDGs
authors: Molla M.H.; Chowdhury M.A.T.; Muhibbullah M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Stakeholder-perception SDG-alignment scorecard (Likert scores across 20 targets/6 SDGs) plus a technical supply-demand gap calculation. Community participation is one Likert item among 20; no specific legal/administrative access mechanism is traced against a household-level outcome.

title: Exploring the role of institutional governance in enhancing sustainability performance of health and sanitation projects in Uganda: a qualitative inquiry
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: Qualitative institutional-theory inquiry (21 interviews with policymakers/health officers/project managers) into how governance shapes project-level 'sustainability performance', not household legal/administrative access. Same author cluster/scope issue as R4F8CFC42FFE1.

title: The Agency, Resources, and Institutional Structures for Sanitation-related Empowerment (ARISE) scales: Psychometric evaluation across eight cities in Asia and Africa
authors: Sinharoy S.S. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Psychometric scale-validation study (EFA/CFA, measurement invariance) of women's sanitation-related empowerment scales. Outcome is scale psychometric performance, not household access/connection/reliability/affordability. Related ARISE cluster papers in pool not yet screened.

title: Enablers and Obstacles in Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) Implementation and Their Contributions to Sustainable Territorial Development
authors: Gallegos A.; Grigg N.S.; Llano W.
exclusion_reason_detail: PRISMA systematic review of 375 IWRM implementation studies at basin/national/transboundary scale, linked to territorial development outcomes. No household-level access outcome examined anywhere.

title: Does Economic Growth Drive Equitable Water and Sanitation Access? Assessing Inequality Reduction Across 64 Nations
authors: García-López M.; López-Ruiz S.; Cuadrado-Quesada G.
exclusion_reason_detail: Cross-country econometric panel (64 nations, OLS/2SLS/SURE) testing GDP growth against aggregate JMP access-rate inequality; unit of analysis is the country, not the household. 'Governance effectiveness' is a generic macro index, not a specific legal/administrative access mechanism. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention.

title: Water Security in Fragile States: Mapping Governance and Water Access in Libya
authors: Ellinport B. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: GIS-based composite water security index (natural availability + infrastructure investment) across Libya's 22 districts from secondary data only. Governance is thematic framing, not a specific access mechanism tied to measured household-level variation.

title: REVISITING: Off-grid, the New Water Supply Solution
authors: Gaudry A.; Colon M.; Baron C.
exclusion_reason_detail: Narrative/critical policy book chapter synthesizing secondary literature on off-grid water solutions; no primary empirical data or systematic review methodology of its own.

title: Drinking Water Quality Regulations: A Contrast Between Germany and Latin America
authors: Vogelmann E.S.; Prevedello J.; Tiruneh G.A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Comparative doctrinal/documentary analysis of drinking-water quality (chemical/microbiological) regulatory standards across countries. Unit of analysis is the legal text, outcome is regulatory stringency, not household access/connection.

title: Institutional trust as a critical determinant of households' willingness to pay for improved water services in Leku Town, Ethiopia
authors: Dumo W.M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Contingent valuation/WTP survey (n=193); institutional trust is an attitudinal/perceptual predictor, outcome is hypothetical willingness-to-pay, not an actual access/connection/reliability/affordability outcome.

title: Water, Sanitation and Health: The World Bank's Financing of Sustainable Development Goal 6
authors: Martínez-Gómez C.; Gallego-Valero L.; Moral-Pajares E.
exclusion_reason_detail: Country/project-level macro analysis of 546 World Bank financing projects using secondary aggregate data; unit of analysis is the country/project, not the household.

title: Knowledge, economic, and WASH challenges affecting menstrual health and hygiene among nursing students in Bangladesh using a mixed-methods approach
authors: Zaman M.N.U.; Sai A.; Yamauchi T.
exclusion_reason_detail: Mixed-methods study of menstrual health/hygiene among nursing students at educational institutions. Population is students, not households; WASH facility adequacy is a campus-level menstrual-management outcome, not household water/sanitation access.

title: Hydro-citizenship revisited: water, belonging, and the politics of adaptation in rough neighbourhoods in the Global South
authors: Bhanye J.
exclusion_reason_detail: Theoretical/conceptual 'Short Communication' re-theorizing hydro-citizenship via flood-adaptation politics; water/sanitation-specific access barriers are named citing another source, not the author's own data. Insufficient information to identify a water/sanitation population/exposure/outcome. Borderline; flagged for reviewer_2.

title: 'No Human Entry' on Paper: Outsourcing Labour, Implementation Gaps, and Everyday Illegality of Manual Scavenging in India
authors: Raj N.; Tiwari M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Secondary-source analysis of caste-based occupational exploitation of manual scavengers (sanitation workers) in India despite legal bans. Population is sanitation workers, outcome is labor exploitation/enforcement of anti-scavenging law, not household sanitation service access.

title: Optimal water tariffs and trade-offs: a multi-objective analysis of municipalities in Pernambuco
authors: De Lima e Silva A.; De Lima e Silva Y.C.; Alcoforado de Moraes M.M.G.
exclusion_reason_detail: Multi-objective optimization model generating a Pareto frontier of optimal water tariffs across 172 Brazilian municipalities. Unit of analysis is the municipality, outcome is a normative tariff-design solution set, not an observed household access/affordability outcome.

title: Resilience and Sustainability Performance of Health and Sanitation Projects in Uganda
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: PLS-SEM survey (n=520 stakeholders: project staff, procurement/technical officers, regulatory officials, beneficiary reps) across 86 health/sanitation projects in Uganda; exposure is organizational resilience (shock absorption, adaptability, redundancy, learning/innovation), outcome is project-level sustainability performance (economic efficiency, social outcomes, environmental management) -- not household-level legal/administrative water/sanitation access. Third paper in the Kyambade et al. project-management cluster (see also R4F8CFC42FFE1, R26FD0045CAAA), same wrong-population/wrong-outcome issue.

title: Institutional conflicts of interest in regional water management: a case study of the water supply in the Taipei metropolitan area
authors: Chen C.-Y.; Cai Y.-S.; Hung Y.-J.; You G.J.-Y.
exclusion_reason_detail: Deterministic WEAP scenario-based hydro-economic simulation of the Taipei metropolitan multi-reservoir water supply system. Exposure/outcome are utility-level pricing, inter-basin transfer-payment mechanisms, and system-wide social loss/shortage under hydrological stress scenarios -- an engineering/economic optimization study, not an empirical household-level access study. Household affordability burden is raised only as a policy-implications discussion point in the conclusion, not measured as data or an outcome variable.

title: Governance, structure, and access: a Bayesian hierarchical analysis of water, sanitation, and hygiene in South Asia
authors: Azimi M.N.; Rahman M.M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Country-level panel analysis (Bayesian hierarchical linear model, 8 South Asian countries, 2000-2024, World Development Indicators data); unit of analysis is the country, not the household. Governance is a composite autoencoder-derived index built from six generic Worldwide Governance Indicators dimensions, not a specific legal/administrative access mechanism tied to household-level outcomes. Same cross-country composite-governance-index pattern as the earlier-excluded Garcia-Lopez (R5E653CCC67DF) and Gallegos (R2D6E5154CE63) papers.
